# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0001 — create seed capability: route-matching tool + 6 targeted policy rules
- Changes I made:
  - tools.py: NEW `get_user_reservations(user_id)` loop/read tool — returns every reservation with origin/destination/cabin/flights in one call (cluster: wrong-reservation selection, tasks 17, 22).
  - policy.md "Execute the action — never stall": mandate the write on the next step after confirmation; treat an explicit, complete, allowed user instruction as the confirmation (cluster: post-consent stall, tasks 40, 25).
  - policy.md "Finding the correct reservation": use get_user_reservations + list_all_airports to match route; never take the first reservation (17, 22).
  - policy.md "Information already on file": DOB/passenger details come from profile/reservation; don't re-ask (22, 11).
  - policy.md "Money, budgets, and reporting amounts": compute with calculate; a stated budget is a TOTAL not per-passenger; decline an upgrade over the cap; state each requested total exactly (tasks 12, 23).
  - policy.md Book flight "copies an existing reservation": reuse existing reservation's flights/dates/cabin/type instead of re-asking (task 25).
  - policy.md Modify-flight Payment: if the requested method is not on file, use the eligible on-file method and do not transfer (task 11).
- Expected effect + why safe: get_user_reservations lets 17/22 act on FQ8APE (EWR→ORD) instead of SEA→DFW. Prompt rules are additive/narrowing; reward is DB×COMMUNICATE with diagnostic-only action checks, so passing tasks 8/19/37 (which pass on final DB state using on-file payment methods, and correctly refuse where required) do not change graded behavior. Verified the new tool runs on all task users and registers (15 tools, schema builds).
- Building on prior RESULTS: none (first iteration). Used cross-run memory: reward=DB×COMMUNICATE; 40/25 stall is a tau2 termination quirk.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still not fully cracked: post-consent stall (40, 25) — the episode can end at "Yes.###STOP###" before the agent gets a turn; only mitigation available is the "explicit instruction = confirmation, act on next step" rule. If this iteration's RESULT shows 40/25 unmoved, the lever to try next is a composite atomic write invoked earlier, or accepting them as simulator-bound.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, look for tool-internal computation clusters (baggage/payment splits) once the behavioral/selection layer is fixed; if rejected, read broke={} and drop the specific regressing edit (most likely suspect: the execute/confirm rule).
